open_decisions.question: S-06-001 (the pure PRULE-021 Source Scope Predicate) is implemented, passes the full gate (rspec 1225/0, brakeman/packwerk/bundler-audit/zeitwerk clean) and is spec-conformant to PRULE-021 as written. Four of five independent adversarial lenses returned PASS; the security lens returned CHANGES_REQUIRED on one verified, LATENT finding: an exclusion bypass via separator-equivalent characters. With include '/' and exclude '/private', the predicate ALLOWS /private%2Fsecret, /private%5Csecret and /private\secret (whereas /private/secret is correctly excluded), because %2F/%5C are correctly not decoded and a raw backslash is passed through, so the exclude segment-boundary test misses; some origins resolve these back to /private/secret. It is spec-conformant (boundary = literal '/'; %2F is reserved and preserved) and latent (the only materialized policy ships exclude_prefixes []; S-06-002/003 excludes and the S-07 crawler are not built). The fix requires either deviating from the ratified PRULE-021 rule (predicate hardening) or an S-07 crawl-behaviour ruling. How should the predicate treat %2F/%5C/raw backslash in exclude (and include) boundary matching?
open_decisions.recommended_option: Option A — ratify a fail-closed hardening of the predicate (treat %2F/%5C/raw backslash as segment separators, or quarantine any path bearing them), applied as a small still-pure addition to S-06-001 with covering tests, and record the deviation from the literal PRULE-021 boundary rule as an ADR + PRULE-021 clarification. Closes the enforcement-kernel gap before excludes ship (S-06-003) or S-07 crawls.
options: A: harden the predicate now (fail-closed) with owner ratification of the PRULE-021 clarification, then move S-06-001 to ready_for_review
B: accept S-06-001 as spec-conformant now (latent) and mandate the hardening as a required predecessor to S-06-003 and S-07
C: rule that S-07 must crawl canonical URLs verbatim (AllowEncodedSlashes off) and reject raw backslash; keep S-06-001 as-is; record the ruling + an S-07 test
